\par\addvspace{10pt}\begingroup\footnotesize\noindent\captionof{table}{Post hoc, added to price every configuration on one scale, with and without a cache discount: cost and latency of every configuration. BIRD development set, \xres{RV2.loop.plus.ex.zs.n} questions, one run per configuration. Upper block: model calls and tokens per question, nominal cost per 1\,000 questions at the DashScope list price of \xres{RV2.cost.price_date} (CNY), priced two ways. With the cache discount: the usage logs record the number of cached prompt tokens, and we apply a price of 0.2 of the input price to those counts; the factor 0.2 is an assumption, not a recorded price. At the full input price: every prompt token at the list input price (no assumption beyond the list price). Every cost and ratio column names which of the two it uses. Wall-clock latency per question is the third group of columns. A configuration is on the Pareto front if no other configuration of any backbone has at least its EX at no higher cost with the cache discount (assumed) and is strictly better in one of the two. Middle block: paired EX difference with a 95\% database-clustered bootstrap interval and, in two columns, the ratio of the cost per question of the other configuration to that of Qwen3.7-Plus single call, once with the cache discount (assumed) and once at the full input price (above one: the other configuration costs more). Lower block: selective answering at three coverage levels, the accepted set being the top share of questions by score, with a 95\% database-clustered interval (ranking recomputed inside every resample) and the routing score costed as part of the run; both cost columns of this block use the cache discount (assumed).}\label{tab:cost}\par\nopagebreak\vspace{2pt}
